1) The surgical management of adrenal metastases from bronchogenic cancer is rarely performed; 2) Adrenalectomy is a feasible and safe procedure for the management of unilateral adrenal metastasis from lung cancer; and 3) Adrenalectomies after lung resection may be an alternative to the simultaneous procedure.
the surgical resection of unilateral adrenal metastases from lung cancer can be a useful procedure for patients who have a good performance status and a limited number of metastases.

the adrenal gland is the most frequent site of metastasis from primary lung cancer, that adrenalectomy can be done with low morbidity and mortality rates, and that adrenalectomies should be performed for patients who are good candidates for surgery.
